Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
1232 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Cooler weather returns this weekend with chances for rain,
  mainly for the eastern plains.

- Still a rather uncertain precipitation forecast for much of the
  I-25 corridor and mountains... but increasing chance for light
  rain/snow Saturday night and again Sunday night.

- A cool start to next week, but a warming and drying trend likely
  by mid-week.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Friday/...
Issued at 1110 PM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Another day closer to this weekend's storm system, and almost all
of the details regarding precipitation potential remain unclear.

We'll start with what we know. A fairly strong surface cold front
is still on track to arrive Saturday morning, sometime not too
long after sunrise for most of the Denver metro. Unlike many of
our cool season fronts, it will take some time to saturate the low
levels, meaning that low/mid cloud cover will be slow to develop 
in the morning before stratus becomes more widespread during the
afternoon hours. High temperatures Saturday afternoon may only
rebound into the low 50s across most of the lower elevations.

Meanwhile, the main upper level low of interest is spinning over
far southern California tonight, and should track off to the north
and east during the day Saturday. Today's trends have been towards
a slower (further west) and slightly stronger low. As a result,
the deeper plume of moisture also ends up a touch further west.
Most of tonight's CAMs throw a large precipitation shield from
south to north during the afternoon and evening hours, with modest
(~0.05-0.25") amounts as far west as the foothills and as far
north as a Longmont - Greeley line. However, most of the
global/regional deterministic guidance is not nearly as bullish
with this potential, nor are most ensemble members during this
time. It will be worth watching if either of these solutions fold
with the 06/12z guidance later tonight. Of note - some of these
wetter solutions also bring in favorable south-southeasterly flow
into Park County where there could be a few inches of snow 
through Sunday AM.

By Sunday, forecast guidance really likes the idea of spinning up
a well-defined Denver cyclone. As noted in the previous discussion,
temperatures will probably warm up into the upper 50s to low 60s 
where clear skies develop, while many locations along the northern
I-25 corridor and northeastern plains remain socked in stratus 
and see temperatures similar to Saturday. The upper low is 
expected to pivot across the region from Sunday afternoon into 
Monday morning. Again, one notable trend is to have this low be 
stronger/better defined, with a negatively tilted trough axis 
noted by Sunday night. As a result, the surface low over eastern 
Colorado ends up a bit more defined and low-level upslope is a 
touch stronger, while QG ascent is placed over our forecast area. 
Again, guidance is all over the place with the actual track of 
both the upper level and surface features. The ECMWF has been 
relatively consistent placing more substantial QPF over our 
central/northern mountains into the adjacent plains, while many of
this evening's CAMs kept most of the meaningful QPF closer to the
CO/WY border. Our preference here was closer the NBM/ECMWF 
ensemble mean, though I would anticipate more changes to the 
forecast over the next 24-36 hours. At the very least, there's two
well-defined periods for potential rain (and mountain snow) this 
weekend for those looking to see their favorite hydrometeors fall 
out of the sky.

Once the trough lifts to the north of our area Monday, we'll re-
enter another period of dry weather through most of the week. Cool
temperatures are still expected to stick around on Monday, with a 
warming trend by Tuesday under a broad warm air advection regime.
Highs most days next week look to be somewhere in the 60s to near
70F.

Forecast confidence does decrease pretty quickly next week. Most 
models show a complex (or simply messy) pattern across most of the
western CONUS. The dominant features will be a couple of strong 
shortwaves/closed lows across the Pacific Northwest and the 
northern Great Plains, with a couple weaker shortwaves associated 
with the subtropical jet. The general pattern supports warm and 
dry conditions, though there could be a couple periods of 
cooler/cloudier weather based on the track of those. There are 
signs that the subtropical jet becomes more active by next 
weekend... but it's difficult to translate that into an actual 
forecast at this time. We'll let this current weekend pass by 
before worrying too much about it.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS through 06Z Sunday/...
Issued at 1130 PM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Current radar shows a northerly boundary pushing across the TAF
sites at this time. As this push comes through, expect a brief
period of ~10-12kt winds, before weakening and becoming light and
variable for a few hours overnight tonight. We may just end up 
holding onto the northerly winds through the night, but speeds are
expected to diminish after this initial push. A cold front is 
still on track to arrive early Saturday morning, with a prefrontal
wind shift returning winds to the NW ahead of the main front, 
between 9-10Z at KDEN, slightly delayed at KBJC and KAPA. Winds 
are expected to increase in magnitude right near sunrise, with a 
more north-northeasterly wind shift expected by 15-16Z. Expect 
some gusty winds (20-25kts) for a few hours behind the front, 
before turning to the northeast for the afternoon. Have pushed the
lower ceilings back by a few hours with this TAF package, as the 
lower levels should take a little while to saturate behind the 
front. We do expect a gradual lowering of ceilings through the 
morning, but with guidance still showing inconsistencies with how 
low ceilings will drop to, confidence is low on whether we end up 
with a period of IFR conditions Saturday evening or not. For now, 
expecting at least MVFR conditions to develop once the lower 
levels are able to saturate, but can't completely rule out a brief
period of IFR conditions developing later in the evening or late 
Saturday night. Confidence in precipitation hasn't grown much from
the PROB30 previously in the TAF, at least for KDEN/KBJC, so have
kept those in place beginning around 21-22Z, with enough 
confidence to bump it up to a TEMPO at KAPA for the late 
afternoon.
